doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Los Angeles, Chet Baker and film beginnings
title: Chet Baker's records: Love, alto flute and Tommyhawk
summary: They discuss the four string charts for Chet Baker, Mandel finishing the bridge of Love, Bud Shank's alto flute, and Chet recording Tommyhawk.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So you’re in L.A., you did the four string charts for Chet Baker, “You Don't Know What Love Is,” , “I love You,” , “The Wind,” which was Russ Freeman's tune and, “Love.”
Yeah, I actually wrote the bridge to that, or finished the bridge for him.
Oh yeah?
Yeah.
It was interesting you used an alto flute on that.
I guess I did, yeah.
With Bud Shank, that’s about the first time I can remember hearing an alto flute on a jazz record.
I guess I just needed something that went lower than the regular flute.
But that was pretty unusual for that time right?
It never occurred to me then I don't think, and I always liked the way Bud played it.
Oh yeah, I love his flute playing.
I do too, I was…
It’s too bad that he stopped.
I was very distressed ‘cause I wasn’t able to use him anymore, he just wouldn’t take flute calls and he was my favorite player.
Yeah, he was a terrific flute player. So also Chet recorded one of your tunes, “Tommyhawk.”
That’s true, he recorded a couple different of my tunes, yeah, “Tommyhawk,” that’s right. You know more about me than I do, so read on.
[laughs] And I guess what a couple years later you did some charts for that record that Chet Baker and Art Pepper did together, The Playboys of jazz, it was a three horn…
It was?
Thing with Chet and Art Pepper and Richie Kamuca.
What’d I write?
I forget.
Oh, you don’t have it here?
No, I don't.
Okay.
That's one thing I didn’t find in the discography.
Well if you can’t help me, I sure can’t.
[They both laugh]
But you did a fair amount, I guess all that was set up through Dick Bock then?
Well some of it, and then one person tells another you know, and so forth.
